en.title: Hiring local staff in ASEAN: laws, bonuses and EoR options
en.standfirst: A guide to hiring staff in Indonesia, Vietnam and the Philippines, covering local workforce requirements, mandatory 13th-month pay and THR, and Employer of Record options.
en.metaDescription: Hiring staff in Indonesia, Vietnam and the Philippines: local labour laws, mandatory 13th-month pay and THR, localisation rules and Employer of Record options.
en.body:
**Hiring local staff in ASEAN** requires country-specific preparation. Home-country employment practices do not establish the rules for a team employed in Indonesia, Vietnam or the Philippines.

For businesses assessing **Southeast Asia employment law**, important planning issues include mandatory allowances, local workforce requirements and the choice of employing structure.

Understanding the **Indonesia THR bonus** and assessing an **Employer of Record in Asia** can help businesses budget and prepare before making an offer.

## Navigating domestic labour laws

There is no single ASEAN-wide employment law governing every regional hire.

Assess the rules in the country where the employee will work, including the relevant local requirements for wages, probation, social security and termination.

Minimum wages can also vary within a country. The Indonesian provincial wage framework makes a single national wage assumption unsuitable for budgeting.

Prepare the employment budget around the applicable location and role. Include statutory allowances and potential termination obligations alongside base salary.

## Mandatory bonuses (13th-month pay and THR)

Indonesia's THR is a mandatory religious holiday allowance for eligible workers.

The Ministry of Manpower's 2026 guidance provides for one month's wages for workers with at least 12 months' continuous service and requires payment no later than seven days before the relevant religious holiday. Eligibility and calculation rules must be checked for other service periods. [Indonesia Ministry of Manpower: THR guidance 2026](https://jdih.kemnaker.go.id/asset/data_puu/2026senaker003.pdf)

In the Philippines, covered rank-and-file employees are entitled to statutory 13th-month pay, payable by **24 December**. It should not be described as an unconditional full extra month's salary for every employee; the entitlement is based on basic salary earned during the year. [Philippines DOLE: 13th-month pay guidance](https://dole.gov.ph/news/dole-to-employers-give-13th-month-pay-on-time/)

Treat these obligations as planned employment costs rather than discretionary bonuses.

## Localisation quotas

Foreign-worker rules and local workforce development requirements need separate attention when a business plans to place expatriates alongside local employees.

Indonesia's framework includes local counterpart training requirements in relevant circumstances. Do not assume one numerical ratio applies to every company or foreign hire.

Before committing to an expatriate role, confirm the current requirements for the position, employer and sector. Avoid using a single assumed local-to-foreign staffing ratio across ASEAN.

## The Employer of Record (EoR) solution

An Employer of Record arrangement may provide a way to employ staff through a local provider while the business assesses its longer-term structure.

Under this model, the provider acts as the local employer and administers payroll and employment compliance, while the client business directs daily work.

Its suitability requires country-specific assessment. Do not assume that an EoR arrangement is available for every role or transfers every legal responsibility away from the client business.

Before selecting the arrangement:

1. Assess whether direct local employment or an EoR suits the planned activities.
2. Confirm the provider's ability to employ the proposed staff lawfully.
3. Budget for statutory allowances and social security costs.
4. Review probation, termination and responsibility allocation.

Indonesia's Ministry of Manpower and the Philippines' Department of Labor and Employment are the agencies identified for their respective employment rules. Establish the local requirements before agreeing to employment terms or a provider contract.

zh.title: 在東協聘用當地員工：法規、獎金與 EoR 選項
zh.standfirst: 在印尼、越南與菲律賓聘用員工的指南，涵蓋當地人力要求、法定第 13 個月薪資與 THR，以及名義雇主（Employer of Record）選項。
zh.metaDescription: 在印尼、越南與菲律賓聘用員工：當地勞動法規、法定第 13 個月薪資與 THR、本地化要求，以及名義雇主（EoR）選項。
zh.body:
**在東協聘用當地員工**需要針對各國分別準備。母國的僱傭慣例並不能決定在印尼、越南或菲律賓聘用團隊所適用的規則。

對於評估**東南亞勞動法規**的企業而言，重要的規劃課題包括法定津貼、當地人力要求，以及僱傭架構的選擇。

了解**印尼 THR 獎金**並評估**亞洲名義雇主**（Employer of Record）方案，有助於企業在發出聘用通知之前做好預算與準備。

## 掌握各國國內勞動法規

沒有一套適用於所有區域聘用的東協統一勞動法。

請評估員工工作所在國的規定，包括工資、試用期、社會保險與終止僱傭的相關當地要求。

最低工資在同一國家內也可能不同。印尼的省級工資框架意味著，以單一全國工資假設編列預算並不合適。

請依據適用的地點與職位編列僱傭預算。除基本薪資外，也應納入法定津貼及可能的終止僱傭義務。

## 法定獎金（第 13 個月薪資與 THR）

印尼的 THR 是針對符合條件勞工的法定宗教節日津貼。

人力部 2026 年指引規定，連續服務滿 12 個月的勞工可獲一個月工資，且必須在相關宗教節日前至少七天支付。其他服務期間的資格與計算規則須另行查核。[印尼人力部：2026 年 THR 指引](https://jdih.kemnaker.go.id/asset/data_puu/2026senaker003.pdf)

在菲律賓，受保障的基層員工有權獲得法定第 13 個月薪資，最遲須於 **12 月 24 日**前支付。不應將其描述為每位員工無條件的整月額外薪資；此項權利是以年度內所賺取的基本薪資計算。[菲律賓 DOLE：第 13 個月薪資指引](https://dole.gov.ph/news/dole-to-employers-give-13th-month-pay-on-time/)

請將這些義務視為已規劃的僱傭成本，而非酌情發放的獎金。

## 本地化配額

當企業計畫讓外派人員與當地員工並肩工作時，外籍勞工規定與當地人力發展要求需要分別處理。

印尼的框架在相關情況下包含當地對口人員的培訓要求。不要假設單一數值比例適用於每一家公司或每一位外籍聘用人員。

在確定外派職位之前，先確認該職位、雇主及產業目前適用的要求。避免在整個東協套用單一假設的本地與外籍員工比例。

## 名義雇主（EoR）方案

名義雇主安排可以讓企業在評估長期架構的同時，透過當地服務商聘用員工。

在這種模式下，服務商擔任當地雇主並處理薪資與僱傭合規事務，而客戶企業則指揮日常工作。

其適用性需要針對各國分別評估。不要假設 EoR 安排適用於每一個職位，或能將所有法律責任從客戶企業轉移出去。

選擇安排之前：

1. 評估直接在當地聘用或採用 EoR 哪一種更適合所規劃的業務活動。
2. 確認服務商有能力合法聘用擬議的員工。
3. 為法定津貼與社會保險成本編列預算。
4. 檢視試用期、終止僱傭及責任分配。

印尼人力部（Ministry of Manpower）與菲律賓勞工與就業部（Department of Labor and Employment）是各自僱傭規定的主管機關。在同意僱傭條件或簽署服務商合約之前，先確定當地要求。
